questions.question: If a sum of ₹1,00,000 is to be paid back in two equal annual instalments at 2frac 3 4 percent compound interest per annum in case of annual compounding, then what is the value of each installment? (Rounded off to nearest integral value)
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Principal sum = ₹1,00,000

Rate of interest = 2.75%

Compound interest and annual compounding.

Concept:

For repayment in two equal annual instalments, each instalment consists of principal as well as interest. For the first instalment, the interest is calculated

for one year, while of the second instalment, it is calculated for two years.

Calculation:

Let P be the value of each instalment.

⇒ According to the concept, we have:

⇒ 100000 = P/(1 + 0.0275) + P/(1 + 0.0275)2

⇒ 100000 = P/(1.0275) + P/(1.0275)2

⇒ 2.0275P = 100000 × (1.0275)²

⇒ P = 100000 × (1.0275)²/2.0275

⇒ P = Rs. 52072

Therefore, the value of each installment is Rs. 52,072.

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a task in 20, 30 and 60 days, respectively. How many days will it take to finish the work if P is helped by Q and R every third day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can complete a task in 20 days,

Q in 30 days,

R in 60 days,

P is helped by Q and R every third day.

**Concept: **

Work done is reciprocal of the time taken. Use the concept of man-days.

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(20, 30, 60) = 60 units

Efficiency of P = 60/20 = 3

Efficiency of Q = 60/30 = 2

Efficiency of R = 60/60 = 1

Work done by P in two days = 2 days × 3 = 6 units.

On third day, all three work together, their combined work = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units.

Therefore, in every cycle of three days, work done = 6 + 6 = 12 units.

To finish 60 unit of work, days required = 3 × 5 = 15 days.

**Hence, it will take 15 days to finish the work.**

questions.question:

2 ÷ (5)/(7) of (7 + 9 × 2) + (15/6 ÷ 5/18 - 24/12)
questions.solution:
**Given: **

2 ÷ 5/7 of (7 + 9 × 2) + (15/6 ÷ 5/18 - 24/12)

**Concept:**

Follow order of operations (BIDMAS/BODMAS): Brackets, Indices/Orders, Division and Multiplication (from left to right), Addition and Subtraction (from left to right).

**Solution:**

2 ÷ 5/7 of (7 + 9 × 2) + (15/6 ÷ 5/18 - 24/12)

⇒ 2 ÷ 5/7 of (7 + 18) + (15/6 × 18/5 - 24/12)

⇒ 2 ÷ 5/7 × 25 + (9 - 24/12)

⇒ 2 ÷ 125/7 + 7

⇒ 2 × 7/125 + 7

⇒ 14/125 + 7 = 889/125

**∴ The simplified value of the given expression is approximately 889/125.**

questions.question: A discount of 4.5 percent is given to the customer on marked price of an article. A girl bought the article for Rs.191. The marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:

A discount of 4.5% is given,

Selling price of the article = Rs. 191

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

Discount = (Discount percentage/100) × Marked Price

**Calculation**:

⇒ 191 = Marked Price - 0.045 × Marked Price

⇒ Marked Price = 191/0.955

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys 10 fans and sells 8 fans at the cost price of 10 fans. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

A shopkeeper buys 10 fans and sells 8 fans at the cost price of 10 fans.

**Concept:**

Profit Percentage = (Profit/Cost Price) × 100.

**Solution:**

The cost price of 1 fan = Selling price of 1.25 fans (since 10 fans are sold for the price of 8, each fan is sold for 1.25 times the cost).

Therefore, the profit per fan = Selling price - Cost price

⇒ 1.25 - 1 = 0.25 times the cost price.

Therefore, Profit percentage = (0.25/1) × 100 = 25%.

**Hence, the profit percentage is 25%.**

questions.question: If A = (2)/(3) B and B = (3)/(5) C, then what is A ∶ B ∶ C?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

A = 2/3 B,

B = 3/5 C.

**Concept:**

Ratio and Proportion method.

**Solution:**

A = 2/3 B and B = 3/5 C,

we can substitute B in terms of C into the first equation to find A in terms of C

A = (2/3) × (3/5)C = 2/5 C.

Hence, A : B : C = 2/5 : 3/5 : 1 = 2 : 3 : 5.

**Hence, A : B : C = 2 : 3 : 5.**

questions.question: Radius of a sphere is 6 cm. The numerical value of the surface area of this sphere is what percentage of the numerical value of its volume?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The numerical ratio of Surface Area to Volume of any sphere is always 3/r.

Required Percentage = (3 ÷ r) × 100

Substitute the given radius r = 6 cm:

Required Percentage = (3 ÷ 6) × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4beee7d06e800082e2269dfbeb8efa08455e15b3b7f86f11a27b3f25638a021.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Radius of the sphere (r) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Surface Area of a sphere = 4 × π × r²

⇒ Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × (6)²

⇒ Surface Area = 144π cm²

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × (6)³

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × 216

⇒ Volume = 288π cm³

⇒ Required Percentage = (Surface Area ÷ Volume) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (144π ÷ 288π) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (1 ÷ 2) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Hemisphere Formulas

The volume of a hemisphere is 2/3 × πr³. Its Curved Surface Area (CSA) is 2πr², and Total Surface Area (TSA) is 3πr².

Surface Area to Volume Ratio

The ratio of the surface area to the volume for a sphere mathematically simplifies to 3 ÷ r. This indicates that as the radius increases, the volume capacity grows significantly faster than its outer surface area.

Total vs Curved Surface Area

For a complete sphere, the Total Surface Area and Curved Surface Area are exactly identical (4πr²) because the continuous shape does not contain any flat base section.
</p

questions.question: Average score of 11 players of a cricket team in a one day match is 32. The runs scored by the ten players are 11, 51, 2, 96, 21, 33, 0, 32, 9 and 14. What is the score of 11th player?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Average score of 11 players is 32,

Scores of ten players are provided.

**Concept: **

Average = Total sum / Number of observations.

**Calculation:**

Total score of 11 players = Average score × Number of players = 32 × 11 = 352.

Total score of 10 players = 11 + 51 + 2 + 96 + 21 + 33 + 0 + 32 + 9 + 14 = 269.

Score of 11th player = Total score of 11 players - Total score of 10 players = 352 - 269 = 83.

**Hence, the score of the 11th player is 83.**

questions.question: There are only two candidates in an election. A person got 40 percent votes and lost by 50 votes. Assuming that there were no invalid votes, the total number of votes are :
questions.solution:
**Given data: **

Candidate got 40% of the total votes and lost by 50 votes.

**Concept:**

If a candidate lost by 50 votes, the winner must have received the remaining votes, which is 60% of the total.

**Calculation:**

Let's denote the total number of votes as 'T'.

So, 60% of T - 40% of T = 50 votes (because the candidate lost by 50 votes).

⇒ 6T/10 - 4T/10 = 50

⇒ 2T/10 = 50

⇒ 2T = 500

Hence, T = 500/2 = 250 votes.

**Therefore, the total number of votes are 250.**

questions.question: On buying 20 bangles, Riya gets 5 bangles free of cost. What is the discount percentage that Riya gets?
questions.solution:
Given:

Riya bought 20 bangles and gets 5 bangles free.

Concept:

Percentage discount = (Free bangles/Total bangles after getting free ones) × 100.

Calculation:

Total bangles after getting free ones = 20 + 5 = 25 bangles.

Discount percentage = (5/25) × 100 = 20%.

Hence, the discount percentage that Riya gets is 20%.

questions.question: A solution consists of 50 litres of pure milk. 10 litres of milk is replaced with equal quantity of water. Again 10 litres of the mixture is substituted by 10 litres of water and this operation is repeated one more time. Find the quantity of milk in the final solution.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial solution consists of 50 litres of pure milk,

Three operations of replacing 10 litres of the mixture with water are performed.

**Concept:**

After each operation, the quantity of milk reduces to (initial quantity - quantity replaced) × (remaining quantity/total quantity).

**Calculation:**

After the first operation, the quantity of milk = 50 × (40/50) = 40 litres.

After the second operation, the quantity of milk = 40 × (40/50) = 32 litres.

After the third operation, the quantity of milk = 32 × (40/50) = 25.6 litres.

**Therefore, the quantity of milk in the final solution is 25.6 litres.**

questions.question: If a natural number when divided by 2,3, and 4 leaves a remainder of 1 in each case, then what is the smallest possible three digit natural number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the LCM of the given divisors: LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12.

The required number will be a multiple of 12 plus the remainder 1: (12 × k) + 1.

The smallest 3-digit multiple of 12 is 108 (since 12 × 9 = 108).

Add the remainder to this multiple: 108 + 1 = 109.

**∴ The correct answer is 109.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 2, 3, and 4

Remainder = 1 in each case

**Formula Used:**

Number = LCM(divisors) × k + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of 2, 3, and 4 = 12

⇒ The required number must be of the form 12k + 1

⇒ We need the smallest 3-digit natural number, so 12k + 1 ≥ 100

⇒ 12k ≥ 99

⇒ k ≥ 8.25

⇒ Since k must be an integer, the smallest possible value for k is 9

⇒ Required number = 12 × 9 + 1

⇒ Required number = 108 + 1 = 109

**∴ The correct answer is 109.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Remainder Concept (Same Remainder)

When a number is divided by x, y, and z and leaves the same remainder r in each case, the general form of the number is: LCM(x, y, z) × k + r

LCM Remainder Concept (Different Remainders)

When a number divided by x, y, and z leaves remainders a, b, and c respectively, and (x − a) = (y − b) = (z − c) = d, the number is of the form: LCM(x, y, z) × k − d

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM
</p

questions.question: A bus covered 60 km at a speed of 15 km/h, 100 km at a speed of 25 km/h and 20 km at a speed of 5 km/h. What is its average speed during the entire journey (in m/sec)?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The bus covered 60 km at a speed of 15 km/h,

100 km at a speed of 25 km/h, and 20 km at a speed of 5 km/h.

**Concept: **

Average speed = Total distance/Total time.

Total distance = 60 km + 100 km + 20 km = 180 km.

Total time = 60 km/15 km/h + 100 km/25 km/h + 20 km/5 km/h = 4 h + 4 h + 4 h = 12 h.

Average speed = Total distance/Total time = 180 km/12 h = 15 km/h

⇒ 15 × 1000/3600 = 25/6 m/sec

**Therefore, the average speed during the entire journey is approximately 25/6 m/s.**

questions.question: The halves of the diagonals of a rhombus are 75 cm and 90 cm. Find its area.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Halves of the diagonals of a rhombus are 75 cm and 90 cm.

**Concept: **

Area of a rhombus = 1/2 × d1 × d2 (where d1 and d2 are the lengths of the diagonals). 

**Calculation:**

The lengths of the diagonals are 2 × 75 cm = 150 cm and 2 × 90 cm = 180 cm.

Area of the rhombus = 1/2 × 150 cm × 180 cm = 13500 cm².

**Hence, the area of the rhombus is 13500 cm².**

questions.question: A thief started running at a speed of 12 m/s, after running for 10 sec a policeman started running to catch the thief in the same direction at a speed of 14.5 m/s. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial distance covered by the thief in 10 sec = 12 × 10 = 120 m

Relative speed of the policeman = 14.5 − 12 = 2.5 m/s

Time required to catch the thief = Distance gap ÷ Relative speed

Time = 120 ÷ 2.5 = 48 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 48 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the thief = 12 m/s

Speed of the policeman = 14.5 m/s

Time for which the thief runs alone = 10 sec

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (in same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time to catch = Distance Gap ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

questions.question: When Ashish finishes a certain work, he gets a total wage of Rs. 70. When Kanika finishes the same work, he gets a total wage of Rs. 165. The daily wages of Ashish and Kanika are Rs. 3.5 and Rs. 5.5 respectively. If both of them do it together, what is the cost of the work?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Ashish's total wage = Rs. 70,

Kanika's total wage = Rs. 165,

Ashish's daily wage = Rs. 3.5,

Kanika's daily wage = Rs. 5.5.

**Concept: **

Total wage = Daily wage × Number of days taken to finish work. 

**Calculation:**

Number of days taken by Ashish to finish work = Total wage/Daily wage = Rs. 70/Rs. 3.5 = 20 days.

Number of days taken by Kanika to finish work = Total wage/Daily wage = Rs. 165/Rs. 5.5 = 30 days.

If both of them do the work together, they can finish it in 1/(1/20 + 1/30) = 12 days.

Cost of the work = Daily wages of Ashish and Kanika × Number of days taken to finish work

⇒ (Rs. 3.5 + Rs. 5.5) × 12 = Rs. 108.

**
;Therefore, the cost of the work is Rs. 108.**
